note: Made-up example episode built on Aesop's public-domain fable 'The Crow and the Pitcher'. Facts are listed but left unchecked on purpose.

core.reason: fable turned true is our 'wrong first' sweet spot

title: The crow in the old fable was real

thumbnail_options.title: A crow can solve this. Can you?
The bird trick from a 2,500-year-old story
Sand vs stones: which raises the water?

logline: When the mess-up can't reach his drink and calls Aesop's crow a fairy tale, the explainer shows the stone trick works - and that real rooks and crows pass the same test.
takeaway: Dropping stones to raise water isn't just a fable: rooks and crows solve it in experiments, and they pick stones over sand.

wants.messup: to finish his drink without listening to a moral
wants.explainer: to let the glass prove the point
wants.asker: to know if the old story is true

beats.text: The mess-up thinks fables are made-up bedtime stories.
He skips the moral and goes straight for the snacks.
His straw can't reach the juice at the bottom of a tall glass.
The explainer drops a pebble in, like Aesop's crow - and he scoffs.
His sand shortcut fails while the stones raise the water.
She shows that real rooks and crows passed the same test - and he becomes a crow, slightly too well.

misconception.belief: It's a fable - birds aren't that clever, and smaller stuff like sand would work better anyway.
misconception.demonstration: sand tube vs stones tube on the bench, then the rook experiment

retention.cold_open: The explainer drops a pebble into a tall glass and says a crow can solve this; the mess-up's straw can't reach.

rehooks.beat: the sand barely moves while the stones tube rises
the mess-up 'becomes a crow' and overfills the glass

shots.speaker: explainer
shots.line: A crow can solve this. You can't. Yet.
shots.visual: Explainer drops a pebble into a tall glass; mess-up's straw can't reach the juice

shots.speaker: messup
shots.line: That's a fable. Birds aren't that clever. Prove it.
shots.visual: Mess-up's straw rattles at the empty top half

shots.speaker: asker
shots.line: Wait. The crow and the pitcher? That really happens?
shots.visual: Asker flips to a fresh page

shots.speaker: messup
shots.line: No. It's a bedtime story. Moral, nap, done.
shots.visual: Mess-up waves the straw dismissively

shots.speaker: explainer
shots.line: Partly. The moral is made up. The trick isn't.
shots.visual: Explainer holds up a pebble
Illustrated page of the old fable: a crow dropping stones into a pitcher

shots.speaker: asker
shots.line: So what's the trick? Drop stones until the water rises?
shots.visual: Asker peers into the glass

shots.speaker: messup
shots.line: Easy. I'll just soak it up with this.
shots.visual: Mess-up plunges a sponge into the glass

shots.speaker: asker
shots.line: The sponge drank it. Now there's even less juice.
shots.visual: The sponge drinks the juice; the level drops further

shots.speaker: explainer
shots.line: You picked the one thing that makes it worse.
shots.visual: Explainer takes the sponge away
Two tubes of water on a bench: one with sand ready, one with stones ready

shots.speaker: explainer
shots.line: Stones push water up. Sand mostly just soaks it in.
shots.visual: Explainer points at the two tubes

shots.speaker: messup
shots.line: Sand is smaller, so it works better. Obviously.
shots.visual: Mess-up pours sand into the first tube

shots.speaker: messup
shots.line: Why isn't it moving? It's tiny! Tiny should be better!
shots.visual: The sand settles; the water barely moves

shots.speaker: asker
shots.line: It barely moved. The stones one is already rising.
shots.visual: Asker points at the second tube

shots.speaker: messup
shots.line: Fine. But a real bird wouldn't know that.
shots.visual: Mess-up folds his arms

shots.speaker: explainer
shots.line: In 2009, scientists asked some rooks exactly that.
shots.visual: Explainer pulls up a tablet

shots.speaker: explainer
shots.line: Each rook got a tube, a floating worm, and stones.
shots.visual: Illustration of a rook beside a tube of water with a floating worm and a pile of stones

shots.speaker: explainer
shots.line: The worm floated too low to reach. So they dropped stones.
shots.visual: Rook drops a stone; the worm rises

shots.speaker: asker
shots.line: They used stones until they could reach the worm?
shots.visual: Asker scribbling

shots.speaker: explainer
shots.line: And they picked big stones over small ones.
shots.visual: Big stone vs small stone side by side

shots.speaker: messup
shots.line: Smarter than me with the sand.
shots.visual: Mess-up stares at his sand tube

shots.speaker: asker
shots.line: Write that down: a bird beat you at physics.
shots.visual: Asker underlines something twice

shots.speaker: asker
shots.line: Do crows do it too, or just rooks?
shots.visual: Asker taps her pen

shots.speaker: explainer
shots.line: Crows do too. Researchers watched them pass the same test.
shots.visual: Illustration of a crow at a water tube

shots.speaker: messup
shots.line: Right. My turn. Pebbles. Big ones. Watch this.
shots.visual: Mess-up gathers a fistful of pebbles
Back at the tall glass: mess-up drops pebbles one by one; the juice climbs

shots.speaker: messup
shots.line: It's rising! I'm basically a crow now!
shots.visual: Mess-up flaps his elbows

shots.speaker: explainer
shots.line: Partly. The crow didn't overfill the glass.
shots.visual: Juice starts spilling over the rim
The glass overflows onto the table

shots.speaker: asker
shots.line: So the fable was right about the trick, not the bird?
shots.visual: Asker wipes the table, notebook safe

shots.speaker: explainer
shots.line: It was right about both. Some birds really do this.
shots.visual: Explainer smiles

shots.speaker: messup
shots.line: Then why did I think fables were all made up?
shots.visual: Mess-up drinks at last

shots.speaker: explainer
shots.line: Some morals are made up. Some observations are older than science.
shots.visual: Explainer pockets a pebble

shots.speaker: asker
shots.line: Things you were wrong about: crows, sand, and juice.
shots.visual: Asker writes; mess-up peers over her shoulder

shots.speaker: messup
shots.line: Partly wrong.
shots.visual: Mess-up's smug grin; cut to black

facts.claim: 'The Crow and the Pitcher' is one of Aesop's fables and is in the public domain.
facts.source: Wikipedia: The Crow and the Pitcher

facts.claim: In 2009, rooks dropped stones into a tube to raise the water and reach a floating worm (Bird & Emery).
The rooks preferred larger stones over smaller ones.
New Caledonian crows have also passed water-displacement tasks.
facts.source: Wikipedia: The Crow and the Pitcher (scientific research)
